lesson_title: Base Before Tower, Tower Before Sheave
hook_text: Two double periods to build a working mine headgear. Here is how a company makes sure nothing is left to chance.
clip_script: Materials list straight off the parts list: dowel in metres, sticks, card, string, gears by tooth count, motor, glue, pins, a little spare on every line, checked against the store today. Tools from what each part needs: saw and bench hook, knives and mats, drill for the shaft holes, clamps, spring balance, stopwatch, eye protection, signed out by name. Then the order, fixed by one question: what must exist first? Cut and label. Base. Gear plate drilled and tested dry. Tower faces flat on the bench, glued square. Stand them, join them, plumb. Tower to base. Back-leg. Sheave. Winder and rope. Brake. Test lifts. Mark what can run in parallel and use the glue time. Draw it as a flow chart with a diamond at every test: gears free? tower square? lifts 300 grams? Then a timetable, fifteen-minute blocks, names across the top, glue before the break, thirty minutes spare.
visual_style: Parts list arrows into a grouped shopping list; a tool tray fills; numbered boxes chain across a whiteboard with two parallel branches; diamonds appear with yes and no arrows; a grid timetable with names fills in.
pacing: Lists, the ordering question, the sequence, the flow chart, the timetable.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw your build's flow chart with three decision diamonds.
